facts.F46: Push point: commit S1, S2, S3 and S4 locally in order and push once after S4. S1 alone is red in CI because the pipelines install SDK 10.0.404, which cannot build net11.0. After S2 the Docker image build, which no required check runs, still uses sdk:10.0. After S3 only the Renovate hold and the prose are left, so one push after S4 gives one CI run and keeps main green. No slice is merged, split or reordered; the order follows the product dependencies.
facts.F47: Version targets: TargetFramework net11.0. Every .NET-versioned package moves from 10.0.15 to 11.0.0, and Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL from 10.0.3 to 11.0.0. The dotnet-ef tool in Lighthouse.Backend/.config/dotnet-tools.json moves from 10.0.15 to 11.0.0, because Create-Migration.ps1 uses it with rollForward false. SDK pin 10.0.404 becomes 11.0.100. Docker tags aspnet:10.0 and sdk:10.0 become 11.0. Packages on their own release trains stay: coverlet.collector, Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing, Serilog.AspNetCore, Serilog.Settings.Configuration, SonarAnalyzer.CSharp, NUnit and adapters, Moq, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, SQLitePCLRaw.
facts.F48: Preservation oracle: the existing backend suite, unmodified, is the behaviour-preservation oracle. NoPendingModelChangesTest is the oracle for "no migration reports a pending model change". If it fails under EF 11, the crafter stops and returns the finding to the architect: a snapshot-only migration is a new decision, not part of this upgrade. Fixtures that say .NET 10.0.0 in SystemInfoControllerTest and in the examine script are values, not pins.
facts.F49: Formal verification: no domain state machine, protocol, concurrency or temporal law is added or changed, so no Quint, TLA+ or Agda model is warranted and no checker is required. Liveness is not applicable: no progress property exists. Safety, inhabitation and reachability are covered by the real build, the existing test suite and the running app, not by a model. Type strength is unchanged. Property-based testing is not applicable, because no input domain or law changes. Jev is unauthorized in this repository: typesafe: unavailable by configuration.
facts.F5: The self-hosted Docker image and the Linux, macOS and Windows standalone builds run on .NET 11 and serve the app.
facts.F50: No ADR: the change makes no durable decision beyond moving to the current runtime. The existing Renovate rule that keeps .NET major image updates manual stays when the hold is removed. Stryker.NET (dotnet-stryker 5.1.0) names no target framework in its per-feature config files, so no config change is needed; whether it runs on a net11.0 test project is checked at the next backend mutation run.
facts.F51: No global.json: CI keeps pinning the SDK through setup-dotnet, which Renovate already updates, so a global.json would be a second authority for the same pin that can drift from it. SDK 11 builds net10.0 projects, so other worktrees still on net10.0 keep working with the newest installed SDK as default. Revisit if a local SDK mismatch causes a real incident.
facts.F52: Input bounds: none are stored or validated by this change. Behaviour-free rule: routes, DTO shapes, serialized responses, UI pixels and topologies stay unchanged. Historical briefs, diagrams and decision records that name .NET 10 stay unchanged. Lighthouse.sln line 5 MinimumVisualStudioVersion is a Visual Studio version and stays. Existing migration Designer files keep their ProductVersion annotations. Adopting new .NET 11 APIs, for example the cookie Partitioned property, is out of scope.
facts.F53: Local toolchain: SDK 11.0.100 and runtime 11.0.0 are installed next to 10.0.114, so S1 can be built and run locally. Docker is installed and the 11.0 images exist, so S3 can be checked locally. No new analyzer warning may be silenced project-wide: TreatWarningsAsErrors is on in Directory.Build.props, so a warning that .NET 11 adds is fixed in code or suppressed narrowly at the call site.
